I'd throw out a couple of things.

First, the way you describe yourself is self-fulfilling. Literally, what you think is who you are. The first step to fixing your problems would be to change how you think about yourself, which can be difficult at first, but is very rewarding. I'd recommend reading As A Man Thinketh, by James Allen. (PDF link here: http://soilandhealth.org/wp-content/uploads/0304spiritpsych/030405thinketh/030405.Thinketh.pdf ) I read the book when I was 19 and it had a really profound impact on my life.

Second, Cincinnati is not necessarily a software development hub. You probably have a fairly unfulfilling job there, which isn't helping. If you can swing it, I'd recommend starting to look into your standard software development hubs like San Francisco and Seattle, and some newer ones like Phoenix or Salt Lake City/Lehi, UT.

Third, your credit will fix itself quickly enough. 7 years and most items drop off, but having a steady income and currently paying your bills goes a very, very long way.

Finally, I'd recommend you start living your life now, instead of waiting. Your life won't suddenly be great when your debt is paid off, or you make more money, or have a better job. It just doesn't work like that. Your life will be great when you start choosing for it to be that way. Pick some hobbies and throw yourself into them. Relish existing hobbies you currently have. Live a bit more in the 'now', and a bit less in the future.

Best of luck to you pal.
